rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity (consolidates front-run check + module-to-module arc + Big Idea fidelity + mood-doesn't-resolve-early).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run: doesn't answer the two frontiers (per watch-for), consistent with M6's Big Idea (two-run gap diagnosis, not frontier-resolution) — no downstream teaching moment spoiled. Arc: correctly sequenced as M6's opener immediately before 'Story of Module 6' per spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md's Start-here link order ([The 2 frontiers] -> [Story of Module 6] -> [Quality is grounding] -> exercise); ends unresolved with no kicker (deliberate, per maintainer note) so it sets up Story of Module 6's non-determinism theme rather than pre-empting it. Big Idea fidelity: stays at horizon-level per its own 'Recap + horizon. Does not teach a new term' role, doesn't restate or contradict M6's Big Idea. Mood-doesn't-resolve-early: leaves the frontiers open through the capstone itself, distinguishing 'practitioner fluency' (a posture: 'I know how to test/learn/encode') from 'having answered the meta-question' (never claimed) — matches the strategy doc's M6 mood definition exactly. CAVEAT (non-blocking, factual accuracy in maintainer block only): both the 'Lecture meta' line and the 'Watch-fors' line call painting-the-picture-with-the-llm.md 'Module 1's Painting the picture closer'. That file's own Meta states 'Role: opener. First lecture of M1' and it is listed first in getting-going.md's Start-here link order (before the wizard-move demo and all three M1 exercises) — it is M1's opener, not its closer. The echo claim itself is accurate and well-built (the two frontier questions recur near-verbatim between the two files); only the closer/opener label is wrong. Maintainer-block-only, no student-facing impact, but worth correcting so a future arc-verification pass doesn't inherit the wrong anchor.
